clients.name: Bump Digital
clients.context:
Bump Digital is the agency Kelsey contracts with; she runs Meta (and proposed LinkedIn) ads for their client Plumbline. KAM contact: Josh Blackman, josh.blackman@bumpdigital.co.nz, 021 840 017.

PLUMBLINE (end client): Bathware/tapware brand, NZ + AU. plumbline.co.nz. Contact: Lauren Rogers, Lauren.rogers@plumbline.co.nz. Existing Google Ads advertiser. New catalogue launches annually (seasonality factor).

BRAND: Pillars = Design, Quality, Choice. B2B pitch (specifiers/architects): design-led product backed by technical resources (3D files, renders, compliance) that keeps projects moving instead of stalling at spec stage. B2C pitch (homeowners): quality bathware that's already resolved (finish, function, durability). Credibility: Lead Free Tapware, Designed in NZ, Manufactured in NZ, Toitu Certified, most complete architectural bathware collection. Competitors: Robertsons Bathware, Elementi, ABI Interiors, Astra Walker, Newtech Bathroomware, Caroma, Duravit, Methven, St Michel Bathroomware, Nero, Bath Co. Full brand guidelines held by Lauren, share on request.

META ADS - CURRENT STATE (Bump Digital's review): 7 campaigns live at $150/day; only 'Book a Consultation - Melbourne' ($50/day) is actionable/lead-generating. The other $100/day (2/3 of spend) is pure brand awareness with no measurable objective - the core inefficiency flagged.

META ADS - PROPOSED GROWTH PLAN: Restructure to $140/day, 100% actionable, across 5 locations (Melbourne/Auckland/Wellington showrooms + NZ & AU national), split B2B (trade/specifiers) vs B2C (homeowners). Showroom 'Book a Consultation' campaigns: $20/day each x3 = $60/day. National product/catalogue campaigns (ecommerce + lead capture): NZ $40/day + AU $40/day = $80/day. Creative needed: Auckland + Wellington showroom graphics, catalogue graphics x8, optional showroom video walkthroughs. Management scope: 7 hrs one-time setup, then 7 hrs/month ongoing (5 management, 1 creative brief, 1 reporting).

LINKEDIN - PROPOSED LAUNCH (new channel, B2B/specifiers): Reuse showroom creative + text-only ads. $60/day (~$1,800/month): 3x consultation campaigns ($10/day each - Melbourne/Wellington/Auckland) + 2x catalogue campaigns ($15/day each - NZ/AU). Setup 6 hrs, then 6 hrs/month ongoing (3 management, 2 creative, 1 reporting).

COMBINED (Meta+LinkedIn): 26 hrs first month with setup, 13 hrs every month after.

CONVERSIONS THAT COUNT: showroom visits, phone calls, ecommerce sales, retail sales, in-person presentations, A&D spec/CAD/sample requests, catalogue requests, quote requests, EDM sign-ups.

EMAIL MARKETING: Not in Bump Digital's initial scope, but Plumbline said yes to wanting help with it (esp. driving ecommerce sales) - a flagged upsell opportunity.

PLUMBLINE'S OWN FY27 MARKETING PLAN (background, not Kelsey's scope): Theme 'Demanding Outcomes'. Audiences: Specifiers (hero focus, 'Win The Specifier'), Homeowners (affluent/designer-led), Retailers (opportunistic). Big projects: Future Website, Catalogue 26/27, AU Market Expansion, Strong Brand in Retail, Lead-Focused Marketing, Product Configurator. Total FY27 media budget: NZ $284K + AU $126K = $410K NZD, across Digital/Social, Print & Editorial, and Partnerships & Events. Plumbline's NZ budget includes a line for 'Bump Digital / Admin - digital management & production fees' at $8,400/yr.

BRAND GUIDELINES (Plumbline, V02): Purpose - 'Enrich the human experience'. Mission - 'To create products and moments of beauty that move you, inspire you, and feel exactly as they should'. Values - World-class, Trusted, Forward-thinking, Customer-focused, Passionate. Brand character - 'the conscious creator', natural integrity + positive agency.

LOGO: Wordmark 'PLUMBLINE' (bold sans, all caps). Secondary lockup adds 'ARCHITECTURAL BATHWARE' beneath. Monogram is a 'ripple' chevron/wave mark, used for constrained formats (favicons, social avatars) and sign-off moments - never as a replacement for the wordmark where space allows.

TYPOGRAPHY: Primary = Material Serif (custom serif, headlines/statement copy/CTAs) - e.g. 'Sanctuary found', 'GET INSPIRED AT PLUMBLINE.CO.NZ'. Secondary = RM Neue (sans-serif) for body copy, sub-headings (often tracked-out caps, e.g. 'POLISHED ORGANIC BRASS FINISH') and annotations.

TONE OF VOICE: Emotive, rhythmic, calm - short evocative phrase triplets separated by the ripple glyph, e.g. 'Sensation on skin > Rewiring something deeper > Your sanctuary' or 'The sleep from your eyes > The fog of old dreams washed clean > Anew for the day'. Used sparingly, with generous spacing - good reference for ad headline/caption structure.

COLOUR PALETTE (hex): Ripple Blue (hero, optimistic/calming) #CDD7DC. Moss (grounding, dark) #233528. Sand (light, warm) #F5F0E6. Clay (warm, dark) #503732. Rule: never pair two light or two dark colours together - always one light + one dark for contrast.

IMAGERY STYLE: Four buckets - (1) Product: 'collection-led' (raw/elemental macro shots of metal + water) and 'product-led' (realistic, soft dappled natural lighting, product in its real setting, not flashy); (2) Place & Space: sanctuary + rejuvenation, warm light, dynamic water always present; (3) Connected Elements: NZ landscapes/water/mountains, supports the elemental world; (4) Plumbline World: behind-the-scenes craftsmanship/team, natural light, realism. Overall feel: warm, elemental, unpretentious sophistication - avoid anything slick/corporate/artificial.

RELEVANCE FOR AD CREATIVE: Match this palette and tone in any Meta/LinkedIn creative for Plumbline - warm natural lighting, close-up material/product detail or genuine lifestyle moments (not stock-photo-clean), Material Serif for any on-image headline, ripple glyph as a small brand device, never two light or two dark colours side by side.

PROJECT PLAN (2026-09-27, updated same day once wardrobe report landed): Duplicate the wardrobe-designer tool/page/outreach playbook for the outdoor/landscape design market.

STATUS: wardrobe build report is in. TECHNICAL FACTS NOW KNOWN (use these, don't re-investigate from scratch):
- Live site thryvegrowth.com = repo 'kelsey-thryve/agency-website' (public), static HTML/CSS/JS, no build step, deployed via GitHub Pages from its default branch 'claude/thryve-growth-website-k83Km' (repo has no 'main'). Hidden pages are a subfolder + index.html (e.g. wardrobe/index.html -> /wardrobe/); reuse style.css tokens + one page-scoped <style> block, add <meta name='robots' content='noindex, nofollow'>, no nav/footer/sitemap entry.
- The actual configurator tool is its own separate repo 'kelsey-thryve/wardrobe-app' (Next.js: photo upload -> AI photorealistic render + AI chat design consultant via Gemini -> chat-refine/re-render -> lead capture form). This is the current/complete reference (ahead of both Drive zips) - for the landscape version, this repo is the one to fork/adapt (new category prompts/UI for garden beds, decking/paving, fencing, premium add-ons), not the zips.
- BLOCKER that will hit the landscape build too: wardrobe-app has never been deployed - needs Vercel (or similar Node/serverless host, not GitHub Pages) + a billing-enabled GEMINI_API_KEY, neither of which exist in this environment yet. The wardrobe page (PR #6, kelsey-thryve/agency-website) shows a 'deploying now' placeholder instead of faking the live embed. Before launching a landscape-app build, confirm with Kelsey whether she's sorted Vercel/Gemini access - otherwise the new demo will hit the identical wall.
- Known bug to avoid repeating: wardrobe-app's AI chat system prompt (app/api/design/route.js) still hardcodes an old placeholder studio name instead of Thryve Growth's actual branding - only the on-page logo was rebranded, not the AI's own identity. Make sure the landscape-app's chat prompt is branded correctly from the start.

Once Kelsey confirms Vercel/Gemini access (or accepts the same placeholder-demo approach for now), brief the website agent (fork wardrobe-app -> landscape-app + build the /landscape page in agency-website) and sales agent (outreach list) in parallel using the decisions below.

TARGET MARKET: broad 'Exterior & Outdoor Design' umbrella - landscapers, garden designers, deck/patio builders, and outdoor living companies together (NZ/AU/US, same geographic spread as the wardrobe outreach list).

TOOL: same underlying container/architecture as wardrobe-app, reskinned with 4 configurable categories: (1) garden beds & planting layout, (2) decking & paving/pathways, (3) fencing & screening, (4) premium add-ons - pergolas, water features, outdoor kitchens.

PAGE: hidden subpage at thryvegrowth.com/landscape (NOT in header/footer/sitemap nav, direct URL only) - same structure as /wardrobe: hero + subtext, a 4-item quick-benefits row, a How It Works step-by-step, the live tool embedded, placeholder before/after photos (no real ones yet), reviews section skipped for v1, and a placeholder 'Book a demo' link pending Kelsey's real booking URL.

COPY - recommended hero: 'Outdoor Spaces Designed For You'. Recommended subtext: 'The ultimate lead generation tool for landscape and outdoor design companies'. Draft benefits row: turns browsers into qualified leads / captures design specs automatically / plugs into any website / books consults with zero back-and-forth. (Kelsey wants fully new/different text from the wardrobe page, not reused copy - confirm final hero/subtext with her before publishing, same as the wardrobe page process.)

OUTREACH: Kelsey confirmed yes to a full duplicate of the wardrobe outreach list (100+ companies, contacts, tailored pitch) for this market - sales agent to build this the same way it built the wardrobe list.

UPDATE (2026-09-28): Kelsey confirmed she'll reuse the SAME GEMINI_API_KEY already deployed for wardrobe-app (same billing project, no new key needed) and will sort hosting herself. Built the landscape-app tool (Next.js, forked/adapted from wardrobe-app) and sent it to her directly as a zip file rather than a GitHub repo - the GitHub integration in this session doesn't have permission to create new repos (create_repository returned 403/404 for both org and personal account). Kelsey will need to push the files to a repo herself if she wants Vercel's git-based deploy, or deploy the folder directly.

WHAT'S IN THE ZIP: full working app - page.jsx UI reskinned for outdoor/landscape (yard photo upload, 6 feature chips spanning all 4 categories: garden beds & planting / deck or paved patio / pathways & stepping stones / fencing & privacy screening / pergola or shade structure / outdoor kitchen or fire feature), api/design/route.js (AI design consultant with a landscape-specific question checklist, correctly branded 'Thryve Growth' from the start - the wardrobe app's branding bug was NOT repeated), api/render/route.js (photorealistic outdoor render prompts adapted from the wardrobe finish/joinery language to landscape materials/hardscaping), api/lead/route.js (same lead-capture pattern, updated copy). README documents reusing the same GEMINI_API_KEY value and includes a .env.example (which wardrobe-app's repo was actually missing despite its README referencing one).

STILL OUTSTANDING: (1) the /landscape hidden page on agency-website itself hasn't been built yet - that's a separate, smaller job for the website agent once Kelsey confirms the hero/subtext copy (drafted in landscapetool001: 'Outdoor Spaces Designed For You'). (2) the sales agent's outreach list for this market hasn't been started yet. (3) once Kelsey has it hosted, get the actual URL from her the same way we got wardrobe-app-seven-cyan.vercel.app, then wire it into the /landscape page and reuse the same booking link (or a new one if she wants a separate calendar).

_syncNote: This file is the shared copy Thryve agents read for business context and write updates to. Seeded from Kelsey's dashboard export on 2026-09-01.
_docsNote: Every client can have uploaded Documents (onboarding forms, briefs, contracts) in the live dashboard's Clients tab. These are stored in the browser's IndexedDB, are NOT included in this data.json export, and are not visible to any agent. If a task needs what's in one of those documents, ask Kelsey to paste the relevant details into that client's Context field (which does sync here) or to share the document directly in this chat — don't assume no documents exist just because none show up here. Prefer saving client documents into the client's Drive folder instead, where agents can read them.
_driveNote: Client data warehouse lives in the private Thryve Growth shared drive, folder 'Client Work' (clientLog.clientWorkFolderId). Each client has a Drive folder (clients[].drive.folderId) with a 'Meeting Notes' subfolder where Gemini meeting notes are filed automatically. The 'Thryve Client Log' Google Sheet (clientLog.sheetId, tab 'Log') is the running record of meetings and work per client: read it (filter by the Client column, using clients[].drive.logLabel) before client work, and append a row after. Detailed client information belongs in Drive, never in this public repo.
_styleNote: House style rule, effective 2026-09-23, for every document/email/ad copy/graphic text any agent produces for Kelsey or her clients: never use an em dash (—). Use a hyphen (-) instead, or rephrase with a comma/period. Applies to all future documents going forward; no need to retroactively fix past docs unless asked.
